title: Distributing a monomial

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying x but leaving the 3 unchanged.
worked_examples.repair: Show two copies of both x and 3, then regroup matching parts.

steps.title: Reach both terms
steps.action: Draw one arrow from 2 to x and another from 2 to 3.
steps.narration: Both parts inside the bracket are doubled.

steps.title: Calculate both products
steps.action: Evaluate 2 times x and 2 times 3 separately.
steps.narration: Two x terms and six units give two x plus six.

worked_examples.repair: Keep the minus sign attached to 4 while each arrow lands.

steps.title: Attach the signed term
steps.action: Multiply 3 by a and by the whole signed value -4.
steps.narration: The minus belongs to four, so the second product is negative.

steps.title: Resolve the products
steps.action: Simplify 3a and 3 times negative 4.
steps.narration: The result is three a minus twelve.

worked_examples.misconception: Applying the minus only to x.
worked_examples.repair: Put a negative badge on each of the two arrows.

steps.title: Send the negative to both terms
steps.action: Place negative two at x and at positive five.
steps.narration: Both terms are multiplied by negative two.

steps.title: Read each signed product
steps.action: Calculate negative two x and negative ten.
steps.narration: A negative multiplier makes both positive bracket terms negative.

worked_examples.misconception: Writing x for x times x.
worked_examples.repair: Use an x-by-x square and an x-by-four rectangle.

steps.title: Partition the area
steps.action: Show the square x by x beside the rectangle x by 4.
steps.narration: Each piece shares the x height.

steps.title: Name both area units
steps.action: Convert x times x to x squared and x times four to four x.
steps.narration: The two areas have different powers and cannot be merged.

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying coefficients but dropping one x in the first product.
worked_examples.repair: Separate coefficient pairs and x factors on the two arrows.

steps.title: Split the rectangle
steps.action: Make a 2x by 3x piece and a 2x by 5 piece.
steps.narration: The common height reaches each width.

steps.title: Expand each factor pair
steps.action: Separate two times three and x times x; then two times five and x.
steps.narration: Only the first region contains two x factors.

steps.title: Name the areas
steps.action: Finish six x squared and ten x.
steps.narration: Different powers describe different area pieces.

worked_examples.misconception: Making the second product negative instead of positive.

steps.title: Attach both signed terms
steps.action: Keep the negative on -3a and on -4 as they pair.
steps.narration: One negative product and one positive product will appear.

steps.title: Multiply the pairs
steps.action: Calculate each sign, coefficient and variable separately.
steps.narration: Negative six a squared plus twelve a remains.

worked_examples.misconception: Missing the middle negative term or the constant.
worked_examples.repair: Use three persistent arrows, one per signed term.

steps.title: Create three paths
steps.action: Connect 4 to 2m, negative 3n and positive 1.
steps.narration: A trinomial has three terms, so the multiplier travels three times.

steps.title: Finish the first path
steps.action: Calculate four times two m.
steps.narration: The first product is eight m.

steps.title: Finish the signed path
steps.action: Multiply four by negative three n.
steps.narration: The second product is negative twelve n.

steps.title: Finish the constant path
steps.action: Multiply four by one.
steps.narration: The last product is positive four.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding exponents to the constant or dropping an x factor.
worked_examples.repair: Count the x factors in each of three paths.

steps.title: Separate the three terms
steps.action: Show an x arrow to every signed bracket term.
steps.narration: None of the three terms can be skipped.

steps.title: Count cubic factors
steps.action: Multiply x by x squared.
steps.narration: One x and two x factors give x cubed.

steps.title: Count square factors
steps.action: Multiply x by negative three x.
steps.narration: Two x factors give negative three x squared.

steps.title: Finish the linear term
steps.action: Multiply x by five.
steps.narration: The constant becomes five x.

worked_examples.misconception: Changing the first sign but leaving the other signs unchanged.
worked_examples.repair: Attach -2y to all three terms and resolve each sign independently.

steps.title: Reach each signed term
steps.action: Draw three arrows from negative two y.
steps.narration: The negative multiplier acts on every term.

steps.title: Resolve the first path
steps.action: Multiply negative two y by positive three y squared.
steps.narration: The first product is negative six y cubed.

steps.title: Resolve the double negative
steps.action: Multiply negative two y by negative four y.
steps.narration: Two negative factors make positive eight y squared.

steps.title: Resolve the last path
steps.action: Multiply negative two y by positive one.
steps.narration: The final product is negative two y.

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying six by two rather than halving it.
worked_examples.repair: Show half of each width in a two-part area model.

steps.title: Split both regions
steps.action: Send one half x to six x and eight.
steps.narration: Halving applies to both bracket terms.

steps.title: Calculate coefficients
steps.action: Take half of six and half of eight.
steps.narration: The coefficients become three and four.

steps.title: Keep the correct powers
steps.action: Place x squared on the first product and x on the second.
steps.narration: Only one region multiplies x by x.

worked_examples.q: A garden is x m wide and (x + 5) m long. Expand an expression for its area.
worked_examples.misconception: Adding side lengths instead of multiplying for area.
worked_examples.repair: Draw an x by x square and x by 5 extension with square-metre units.

steps.title: Partition the garden
steps.action: Divide the long side into x metres and five metres.
steps.narration: The common width x is multiplied by both pieces.

steps.title: Count square metres
steps.action: Add the two region areas.
steps.narration: The square has area x squared and the extension has area five x.

worked_examples.verify: At x=3 m: original area 3·8=24 m² and 3²+5·3=24 m².

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying 2x by three although it lies outside the bracket.
worked_examples.repair: Draw a boundary around the bracket; the outside 2x remains untouched.

steps.title: Respect bracket boundary
steps.action: Send three only to x and two inside the bracket.
steps.narration: The separate plus two x stays outside the distribution.

steps.title: Finish the constant
steps.action: Evaluate three times two.
steps.narration: The constant contribution is six.

steps.title: Collect matching x terms
steps.action: Join three x and two x.
steps.narration: Five x and six are unlike terms, so keep both.

worked_examples.misconception: Treating -4b as positive inside the bracket.
worked_examples.repair: Show the signed term cards before the three arrows land.

steps.title: Separate every signed term
steps.action: Draw a path to 3a, -4b and +5.
steps.narration: The sign stays attached to its own term.

steps.title: Finish a path
steps.action: Calculate negative two times three a.
steps.narration: The first term is negative six a.

steps.title: Use the double negative
steps.action: Calculate negative two times negative four b.
steps.narration: The second term is positive eight b.

steps.title: Finish the constant
steps.action: Calculate negative two times five.
steps.narration: The last term is negative ten.

worked_examples.q: A learner claims 2(x + 3) = 2x + 3. Find the first wrong step and repair it.
worked_examples.misconception: Checking only the x part of a claimed expansion.
worked_examples.repair: Compare the claimed route and two correct arrows with the undoubled 3 marked.

steps.title: Compare both routes
steps.action: Put the learner claim beside an arrow for each bracket term.
steps.narration: The claimed route has only one completed multiplication.

steps.title: Locate the first mistake
steps.action: Highlight the second path, where three was copied unchanged.
steps.narration: Two must multiply three as well as x.

steps.title: Repair and check
steps.action: Replace the incorrect constant by six.
steps.narration: The correct expansion is two x plus six.

worked_examples.verify: At x=1: original 2(1+3)=8, wrong claim 2(1)+3=5, repair 2(1)+6=8.

worked_examples.misconception: Failing to subtract both terms from the second product.
worked_examples.repair: Keep two bracket strips separate, then place negative badges on both second-strip products.

steps.title: Expand each bracket independently
steps.action: Draw two arrows from 2x and two arrows from x.
steps.narration: Each multiplier acts only within its own bracket.

steps.title: Subtract the whole second expansion
steps.action: Distribute the minus to x squared and to negative two x.
steps.narration: The minus reverses both signs in the second group.

steps.title: Collect like powers
steps.action: Combine two x squared minus x squared, and six x plus two x.
steps.narration: The simplified result is x squared plus eight x.

practice_questions: A negative factor reaches both terms.
y multiplied by y gives y squared.

Three x lies outside the bracket.

mastery_questions: Negative four times negative three is positive twelve.
First term contains x·x; second contains one x.
Three arrows produce three signed products.
x² + 9x; at x=2 both forms equal 22.
reassessment_questions: Negative five times negative two is positive ten.
Four a times a is four a squared; four a times three is twelve a.
x² + 13x; at x=2 both forms equal 30.
